issue.summary: Same supplier on 3 different payment terms across ERPs

plan.diagnosis: Zenith Pacific Energy AG is configured with inconsistent payment terms across three ERPs (Oracle EBS: 'Net 30', NetSuite: 'NT30', SAP: 'NET 45'), creating cash flow unpredictability and potential supplier relationship friction. The $18,087,729 annual spend across these systems is being paid on different cycles, preventing leverage of working capital optimization and volume-based payment negotiations.

remedy_steps.step: Convene cross-functional team (AP, Procurement, Treasury) to analyze Days Payable Outstanding impact and establish standard payment term of Net 45 for Zenith Pacific Energy AG across all ERPs to maximize working capital while maintaining supplier relationship
Negotiate formal amendment to master supply agreement with Zenith Pacific Energy AG confirming Net 45 terms globally, securing early payment discount of 2% for payment within 10 days as alternative
Update supplier master data in Oracle EBS (change 'Net 30' to 'NET 45'), NetSuite (standardize 'NT30' to 'NET 45'), and validate SAP 'NET 45' configuration in vendor master
Implement automated three-way match tolerance and payment term validation rule in Coupa to flag future payment term discrepancies for Zenith Pacific Energy AG invoices across all ERP sources
Communicate standardized payment terms to all AP teams processing Zenith Pacific Energy AG invoices and conduct reconciliation of in-flight invoices to ensure correct term application

plan.expected_impact: Standardizing payment terms will improve Days Payable Outstanding by approximately 10 days on $12,058,486 currently on shorter terms (Oracle EBS and NetSuite non-Net 45 spend), generating approximately $33,496 in working capital benefit annually at 10% cost of capital, with potential additional savings of $361,755 if 2% early payment discount is captured on 10% of $18,087,729 spend.
kpis: Payment term compliance rate for Zenith Pacific Energy AG across all ERPs (target: 100%)
Days Payable Outstanding for Zenith Pacific Energy AG (baseline vs. post-harmonization)
Invoice processing cycle time variance reduction (target: <5% across ERPs)
Early payment discount capture rate (target: 10% of invoice volume)
Supplier master data accuracy score for payment terms field (target: 100%)
risks: Zenith Pacific Energy AG may resist Net 45 extension from current Net 30/NT30 terms, potentially requiring concessions
In-flight invoices with mixed terms may create short-term AP confusion and payment delays during transition
ERP master data governance gaps could allow future term mismatches if change controls are not enforced
Extending payment terms may strain supplier relationship if not communicated with early payment discount alternative
erp_actions: Oracle EBS: Update supplier site payment terms from 'Net 30' to 'NET 45' in AP_SUPPLIER_SITES_ALL table for Zenith Pacific Energy AG
NetSuite: Change vendor record payment terms from 'NT30' to 'NET 45' and update all subsidiary assignments
SAP: Validate existing 'NET 45' configuration in LFB1 (vendor company code data) for Zenith Pacific Energy AG; ensure ZTERM field consistency across all company codes
Coupa: Create supplier-specific validation rule to enforce 'NET 45' payment term on all POs and invoices for Zenith Pacific Energy AG across all ERP sources
All ERPs: Implement master data governance workflow requiring dual approval for any future payment term changes to Zenith Pacific Energy AG
SAP/Oracle/NetSuite: Add vendor master data audit report to monthly compliance dashboard tracking payment term consistency for top 100 suppliers by spend
